name: LittleBig Universal CalDAV for FluentBooking
author: André Daus

sections.description:
LittleBig Universal CalDAV for FluentBooking adds a generic CalDAV driver to FluentBooking Pro, allowing you to sync bookings with any CalDAV-compliant calendar server.

Supported CalDAV servers:

  • Zoho Calendar (.com, .eu, .in, .au, .jp, .uk, .sa, .ca datacenters)
  • Fastmail
  • iCloud (via CalDAV)
  • Any RFC 4791-compliant server

Features:

  • Automatic event creation when a booking is scheduled
  • Event updates on reschedule
  • Cancellation sync (STATUS:CANCELLED) to preserve calendar history
  • Hard delete on booking deletion
  • Conflict-checking (checks remote calendar for busy slots)
  • HTTP Basic Auth — each host connects with their own username and password (or app password)
  • Credentials stored encrypted using libsodium
  • Supports multiple CalDAV connections per host user

Requirements:

  • WordPress 6.0 or higher
  • PHP 8.3 or higher
  • FluentBooking Pro 1.2.4 or higher
  • libsodium PHP extension (bundled with PHP 7.2+)
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate FluentBooking Pro first.
  2. Upload the littlebig-universal-caldav-for-fluentbooking folder to /wp-content/plugins/, or install via Plugins > Add New.
  3. Activate the plugin.
  4. Go to Settings > Integrations > CalDAV (Generic) and enter your CalDAV server base URL (e.g. https://calendar.zoho.eu/caldav). This is set once by the site administrator and shared across all hosts.
  5. Each calendar host goes to FluentBooking > Host Settings > Remote Calendars, selects CalDAV (Generic), and clicks Connect CalDAV Calendar.
  6. Enter the host’s CalDAV username and password (or app password — see the FAQ for Zoho Calendar).
sections.faq:
How do I connect Zoho Calendar?

  1. In your site’s WordPress admin, go to Settings > Integrations > CalDAV (Generic) and enter your Zoho CalDAV base URL. Use the URL that matches your Zoho datacenter:
    • https://calendar.zoho.com/caldav — Americas / default
    • https://calendar.zoho.eu/caldav — Europe
    • https://calendar.zoho.in/caldav — India
    • https://calendar.zoho.com.au/caldav — Australia
    • https://calendar.zoho.jp/caldav — Japan
    • https://calendar.zoho.uk/caldav — United Kingdom
    • https://calendar.zoho.sa/caldav — Saudi Arabia
    • https://calendar.zohocloud.ca/caldav — Canada
      Use the server root exactly as shown: no trailing slash, and no calendar ID or /events/ path after /caldav.
  2. Each host generates a Zoho app password: log in to myaccount.zoho.com, go to Security > App Passwords, and create a new password for CalDAV access.
  3. In FluentBooking > Host Settings > Remote Calendars, select CalDAV (Generic) and enter the Zoho email address as the username and the app password as the password.

What is an app password and why do I need one?

Some CalDAV servers — including Zoho Calendar — do not accept your main account password for CalDAV access. An app password is a dedicated token you generate in your account security settings. It works only for CalDAV and can be revoked independently of your main password.

Is this plugin GDPR-compliant?

This plugin is designed with GDPR in mind. Here is a full breakdown of how it handles personal data:

Personal data transmitted

When a booking is created, updated, cancelled, or deleted, the plugin sends the following data to the CalDAV server you configure: attendee name, attendee email address, booking start/end time, and any booking notes. No other personal data is transmitted. Nothing is sent to the plugin author or any third party.

Data stored locally (WordPress user meta)

The following values are stored in WordPress user meta for each calendar host:

  • Encrypted CalDAV credentials (username and password or app password)
  • CalDAV server URL and discovered calendar list
  • Per-booking event URL and UID (used for updates and deletion)
  • A flag indicating whether a connection needs re-authorisation

All credential values are encrypted with libsodium (sodium_crypto_secretbox) before storage. They are never stored in plaintext.

Data deletion

When the plugin is deleted (not just deactivated), uninstall.php removes all plugin user meta for every user. You can also disconnect an individual host at any time via FluentBooking > Host Settings > Remote Calendars, which deletes that host’s credentials and cached calendar data immediately.

Your CalDAV server as a data processor

The CalDAV server you connect to (e.g. Zoho Calendar, Fastmail, iCloud) receives and stores personal data from your bookings. As the site owner and data controller, you are responsible for ensuring that server complies with applicable data protection law and that you have a lawful basis for transferring attendee data to it. Review the privacy policy of your CalDAV provider before use.

No telemetry

This plugin makes no outbound requests except to the CalDAV server URL you explicitly configure. No usage data, error reports, or analytics are sent anywhere.

Does this require the Nextcloud Calendar integration?

No. This plugin is completely independent from the Nextcloud Calendar integration included with FluentBooking Pro. You can use both simultaneously.

Where do I report security bugs found in this plugin?

Please report security bugs found in the source code of this plugin by email to security@littlebig.co. We acknowledge every report within 48 hours.

Please do not open public issues or post vulnerability details in support threads. Our full policy: https://littlebig.co/policies/security/
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • Fix: a trailing slash on the CalDAV server URL (for example https://calendar.zoho.eu/caldav/) made Zoho Calendar reject the connection with “could not discover principal URL”. Discovery now tries the URL without a trailing slash first and falls back to the URL as entered, and the error message explains what the server URL should look like.
  • New: Zoho Calendar UK (.uk), Saudi Arabia (.sa) and Canada (.ca) datacenters are listed in the documentation.
  • Fix: when a booking is being made, the conflict check now queries the calendar server directly instead of using the cached result, so an event added moments ago still blocks the slot.
  • Fix: if the calendar server cannot be reached while a booking is being made, the plugin now falls back to the last known conflicts and no longer caches the failed result, so a server hiccup cannot make a busy slot look free.
  • Improvement: when an update to a calendar event is skipped (no linked event, lost connection or failed authentication), the reason is now written to the booking activity log. Failed conflict-check requests are written to the PHP error log when WP_DEBUG is on.
  • New: security reporting channel (security@littlebig.co) added to the FAQ, the repository and the Plugins screen. No change to plugin behaviour.

1.0.6

  • Fix: event descriptions with line breaks were double-escaped, so calendar apps (reported with SOGo) displayed literal \n instead of a line break. FluentBooking hands the plugin a description already escaped for its own raw .ics builder; the plugin’s underlying iCalendar library was escaping it a second time. The description is now unescaped before being handed to the library, so it is only ever escaped once.

1.0.5

  • Fix: the VEVENT sent to the CalDAV server contained a duplicate UID and DTSTAMP property (RFC 5545 §3.6.1 requires each exactly once). Caused by the underlying Sabre library auto-generating its own UID/DTSTAMP defaults, which were never removed before the plugin added its own values. Most servers accepted the malformed event (some with a validation warning), but stricter RFC 5545 validation could reject it outright. Found and diagnosed via a beta tester’s raw traffic capture against Infomaniak’s CalDAV server — thank you.

1.0.4

  • New: events now include a VTIMEZONE component with the host’s timezone, and DTSTART/DTEND use TZID instead of UTC-only. Some CalDAV servers display raw UTC in their own generated calendar invitations (when “Attendee Notifications” is set to let the server send them) — a proper TZID gives those servers the information they need to show the correct local time instead. RFC 5545 §3.6.2 compliant.

1.0.3

  • Fix: some CalDAV servers (Infomaniak, and others that perform server-side scheduling) sent their own iMIP invitation email to the attendee — in addition to the FluentBooking confirmation email — and displayed the event time in UTC instead of local time. The ATTENDEE property now sets SCHEDULE-AGENT=CLIENT (RFC 6638), which tells the server not to send its own scheduling messages.
  • New: “Attendee Notifications” option under Settings → Integrations → CalDAV (Generic) — “Let FluentBooking handle notifications” is enabled by default; disable it to restore the CalDAV server’s own invitation emails.

1.0.2

  • Fix: fatal error getBookedSlots(): Argument #5 ($host_id) must be of type ?int, string given when opening the “add booking manually” panel in the FluentBooking admin, on FluentBooking 2.2.0+. FluentBooking does not always pass an int/null for the host ID argument on this and several related hooks; those arguments are now normalized defensively instead of strictly typed.

1.0.1

  • Fix: “CalDAV PROPFIND returned unexpected status 200” error when connecting to servers (e.g. Spacemail) that respond to PROPFIND/REPORT with HTTP 200 instead of the RFC 4918 standard 207 Multi-Status.
  • Fix: fatal error when saving a connection with no conflict-check calendars selected (patchConflictSettings(): Argument #1 must be of type array, null given).

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Generic CalDAV driver with HTTP Basic Auth and app password support.
  • Central server URL configured once by the administrator; each host authenticates individually.
  • Full booking lifecycle sync: create, update, cancel, delete.
  • Conflict checking with transient caching.
